Does anyone else find it *easier* to eat when watching My 600 lb Life and other shows that feature enormous beasts killing themselves with food? (I feel kinda bad comparing things that used to be human to other beasts; almost all actual beasts will stop eating before they become engorged and choose to engage physically with their environment rather than eat more when they are not held captive.) I do, and it seems counter-intuitive: most posts about such shows elicit responses about how much seeing the subjects eat kills viewer appetites.

Food really doesn't interest me, and I think it's normal to not eat until I am hungry enough to actually feel stomach pain. It's kind of like how little kids don't want to go to sleep because being awake is too interesting - the whole process of eating, much less prepping, cooking, eating, and clean-up, is arduous and boring. After some trial and error, and a few hospitalizations for genuine exhaustion and dehydration (*not* anorexia: though I have much respect for people battling that illness, it's completely different), I've learned to keep a few reliable, nourishing staples around that can be prepared and ingested with little effort.

The idea of eating for fun seems as wasteful as wiping your ass with money. Watching freak-show-fat people eat on TV, though, must spark some self-destructive mimicry program nestled in my greasy reptile brain: they eat so many things that I never think about and even use their limited energy to *make* particularly desired food items, going so far as to deep fry chicken and won tons in their beds. Watching them tuck into heaping plates of waffles soggy with syrup topped with fried "chikken" (foods I don't even like), I'm reminded that it's been a while since I ate and defrost a donut or two, make a cup of tea, and might even order a pizza with dessert.

Does anyone else experience something like this? Are binges contagious, or contagious only if you're already operating below your daily calorie needs?
